rv.q: And what Rambert is now is loud, fast, brash and rather superficial, if this fleetingly enjoyable take-away meal of an evening is what we have to go on.
This is all very good, and everything tonight is good, even if only some of it really thrills – that’s the necessary risk of new work.
It was a thrilling, beautiful and moving evening which really allows this talented company to shine.
A very diverse mixed bill for Fall for Dance showed some top notch dancing though it was not entirely successful choreographically.
The piece feels intimate, showcasing the dancers’ exquisite fluidity and linework, while flashes of humour emerge through sharp, staccato gestures.
The raw energy of this piece, animated by Pierre Aviat's assertive, pounding musical score, is contagious, and the dancers' sheer joy and togetherness make for a thrilling half-hour.

cn.t: Rambert's centenary celebration earns praise for its forward-looking vision, showcasing bold, high-impact contemporary works that reflect the company's present evolution rather than dwelling on nostalgia.
